**SEC-05** · warning · [Verified] — `index.html` loads fonts from `fonts.googleapis.com`
at runtime. The page depends on a third party staying available, and visitor IP addresses
reach Google on every page load — a privacy consideration in some jurisdictions.
**Fix:** download the two font files into `assets/` and reference them locally.

*Not applicable here: BUILD (nothing to install, build or pin), RUN (no server process),

## 2. How does the deployment work?

Every push to `main` rebuilds the set of files that belong in production and copies them
onto the Azure web server.

1. **Checkout** — GitHub takes a fresh copy of the repository.
2. **Assemble payload** — copies `index.html`, `scrub-engine.js` and `assets/` into a
   folder called `site`. The Python generators in `build/` and the 7 MB demo video in
   `docs/` are deliberately left out; a web server has no use for either.
3. **Verify assets** — reads every `assets/...` path referenced by `index.html` and fails
   the run if any file is missing. This catches a broken deploy before it ships, not
   after.
4. **Deploy** — downloads that exact payload and uploads it to App Service using the
   publish profile. It deploys what was built; it never rebuilds.
5. **Health check** — requests the live site up to 10 times over ~2.5 minutes and fails
   the run unless it gets HTTP 200.

The deploy job runs in a GitHub Environment named `production`. If you add required
reviewers to that environment, deployments will wait for approval.

**If any step fails the run stops** — a failed build never reaches Azure.

## 3. What do I need to configure?

One-time setup, done by a person.

### GitHub secrets

Repository → **Settings** → **Secrets and variables** → **Actions** → **New repository secret**.

> Secret values never appear in this document and must never be pasted into chat.

| Secret name | What to put in it | Where to get it |
|---|---|---|
| `AZURE_WEBAPP_PUBLISH_PROFILE` | The whole contents of the publish profile file | Azure Portal → your Web App → **Get publish profile** (downloads an XML file) → open it and copy everything |

### Azure resources

**[Unknown]** — the skill cannot see your Azure account and cannot check these exist.

| Resource | Name | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| App Service | `scrool-world-app` | Must exist before the first push. The name is also the public address. |

### Publish profile setup

1. Azure Portal → your Web App → **Get publish profile** (top toolbar). An XML file downloads.
2. Open it in a text editor, select all, copy.
3. Paste into the GitHub secret named above.
4. **Re-download and update the secret whenever the app's publishing credentials are
   reset** — the old profile stops working immediately and the deploy will fail with 401.

### ⚠ Startup command — you must set this by hand

A Linux App Service will not serve these files on its own, and **a publish profile cannot
set the startup command** — the workflow has no way to do it for you.

Azure Portal → your Web App → **Configuration** → **General settings** → **Startup Command**:

```
pm2 serve /home/site/wwwroot --no-daemon --spa
```

Two alternatives that avoid this entirely: create the App Service on the **PHP** stack, or
on **Windows**. Both serve static files from the deployment folder with no startup command.

### Before the first push

- [ ] Confirm the name `scrool-world-app` is spelt as intended — it becomes
      `scrool-world-app.azurewebsites.net` and cannot be renamed later
- [ ] Azure resource `scrool-world-app` exists and is running
- [ ] An App Service Plan has been chosen (free F1 is enough for static files)
- [ ] Secret `AZURE_WEBAPP_PUBLISH_PROFILE` has been added
- [ ] Startup command set, or the app is on the PHP/Windows stack
- [ ] No app settings are needed — this site reads no environment variables [Verified]
- [ ] Someone has read `.github/workflows/deploy-app-service.yml` and agrees with it

## 4. How do I run the deployment?

Finish the checklist above, then:

```bash
git add .
git commit -m "Add Azure deployment workflow"
git push origin main
```

The workflow starts automatically. To deploy without pushing, open the **GitHub Actions tab**,
choose **Deploy to Azure App Service** in the left sidebar, and press **Run workflow**.

**No Azure commands needed.** The workflow does that; section 3 is one-time.

---

## 5. How do I know whether it succeeded?

1. Open the **GitHub Actions tab** of this repository — labelled **Actions**, along
   the top of the repo page.
2. Click the latest run of **Deploy to Azure App Service**.
3. Green tick = every step passed. Red cross = click the failed step for the log.
4. Then open https://scrool-world-app.azurewebsites.net

The workflow already checks this for you: the final step polls the site and fails the run
if it never returns HTTP 200. A green tick therefore means the page responded, though it
does not prove the video clips play correctly.

### Already checked

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| YAML parses, required keys present | Passed |
| All 4 action references pinned to a version | Passed |
| Permissions least-privilege (`contents: read`, no unused `id-token`) | Passed |
| No inline credential literals | Passed |
| No unsubstituted template tokens | Passed |
| `concurrency:` set — simultaneous deploys prevented | Passed |

16 checks passed, 0 failed.

**Not performed:** actionlint expression checking (not installed on this machine);
whether the Azure resource exists, has the right stack, or the identity may deploy to it
(no Azure access); whether the GitHub secret exists (no repository settings access);
whether the site actually serves traffic (not executed).

> YAML validation confirms syntax and structure only. It does not prove the deployment
> will succeed. Azure resources, permissions, quotas and network paths are unverified.

### If it fails

| Symptom | Likely cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Deploy step fails with 401 or 403 | Publish profile expired or credentials were reset | Re-download the publish profile and update the secret |
| Deploy succeeds, health check fails with 403 or 404 | No startup command on a Linux App Service, so nothing is serving `wwwroot` | Set the startup command in section 3, or move to the PHP/Windows stack |
| Page loads but every scene is blank | The host is not serving `.mp4` files, or is not honouring byte-range requests | Check the browser Network tab for the requests to `assets/vid/` |
| Build fails at "Verify every referenced asset" | An `assets/...` path in `index.html` points at a file not committed | The log names the missing file; commit it or fix the path |
| Page loads but fonts look wrong | `fonts.googleapis.com` unreachable | Expected — see the SEC-05 warning in section 1 |

Re-check anytime with `/deploy-check validate`.
